mclaren health plan.how: McLaren posts a no-login InterQual viewer. Open the link, then find the subset for your surgery. It is read-only, so screenshot the criteria page — you'll want it attached to the appeal.

medical mutual of ohio.how: Medical Mutual uses InterQual first and MCG second, and publishes a no-login viewer for BOTH. Try the InterQual link first; if your surgery isn't there, use the MCG one.
medical mutual of ohio.source: medmutual.com 'Medical Necessity Criteria and Clinical Review Guidelines'

ucare.how: UCare posts a no-login InterQual viewer.
ucare.warning: UCare Minnesota was placed into court-ordered receivership on 17 Dec 2025 and appeal deadlines have been changed by court order. Read the 'UCare Minnesota - In Receivership' notice on ucare.org BEFORE you file, so you don't miss an amended deadline.

viva health.how: Viva posts a no-login InterQual viewer (CMS requires it for Medicare Advantage). If the surgery isn't listed, call and ask for the specific InterQual subset used on your denial.

communitycare.how: CommunityCare posts a no-login InterQual viewer. Note they announced a move to MCG on or after 1 Aug 2026 - ask which set applied on YOUR decision date.

quartz health plan.how: Quartz posts a no-login MCG Cite viewer. Find the guideline for your surgery and screenshot it.

oklahoma medicaid (soonercare).how: Oklahoma's Medical Authorization Unit reviews surgical PA using InterQual and posts a public transparency link.

health alliance plan (hap).how: HAP gates InterQual behind a login you must request. Email InterQualReq@HAP.org and ask for access, or ask directly for the InterQual subset used on your denial. If you're on HAP CareSource Marketplace, your surgery went through TurningPoint instead - call (866) 422-0800 and request a digital copy of the policy.

molina healthcare.how: Molina's own utilization-management page says criteria are MCG behind the secure provider portal, AND that you may phone to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. Ask for 'the MCG guideline title and criteria applied to my determination'.
molina healthcare.warning: Molina's shoulder arthroscopy policy MCP-404 was RETIRED on 12 June 2024, but old copies still load at several molinahealthcare.com URLs. If anyone cites MCP-404 at you, it is not current policy.

community health plan of washington.how: CHPW publishes its own criteria for most joint surgeries (ask for the 'MM' policy number for your procedure). Two policies exist but aren't posted publicly - MM183 cervical/lumbar fusion and MM186 hip FAI - request those by phone.
community health plan of washington.source: CHPW Clinical Coverage Criteria index, updated 7 Aug 2026

geisinger health plan.how: Geisinger delegates musculoskeletal review to Cohere Health and publishes no orthopedic criteria. Pennsylvania Act 146 requires them to disclose the basis for a denial - ask for 'the Cohere clinical guideline applied to my authorization'.

capital blue cross.how: Capital delegates all musculoskeletal surgery to TurningPoint. Their criteria aren't downloadable - use the contact form on the TurningPoint page naming Capital Blue Cross, or call, and ask for the medical policy used on your denial.

common ground healthcare cooperative.how: Administered by CareSource with TurningPoint doing musculoskeletal review. Wisconsin line is (414) 296-6120.

priority health.how: Priority Health publishes real policies (91571 knee, 91581 spine) but they hand the actual medical rules to TurningPoint. Quote the Priority policy number in your appeal AND request the TurningPoint criteria - via the form on their page or through Priority's Prism portal (Authorizations > Authorization Criteria Lookup).

mountain health co-op.how: Mountain Health CO-OP's utilization management is run through University of Utah Health Plans. Their provider manual states criteria can be obtained by contacting the UM team at that number or email - do exactly that.
mountain health co-op.source: Mountain Health CO-OP Provider Manual, June 2024

iowa total care.how: Iowa Total Care routes shoulder/hip/spine/knee surgery to Evolent, whose criteria ARE public on RadMD at no charge. Confirm with provider services that your code went through Evolent, then pull the 2026 Evolent Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines.

vantage health plan.how: Vantage names no criteria vendor publicly and their site blocks automated access. Call and request the written criteria relied on. For Medicare Advantage plans, CMS rules require them to disclose the internal coverage criteria used.

_evolent.how: Your plan uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery, and Evolent publishes its criteria free with no login. This is the exact document your reviewer used.

_carelon.how: Your plan uses Carelon for musculoskeletal surgery, and Carelon publishes all of its guidelines free with no login. Open the current Joint Surgery, Spine Surgery or Small Joint Surgery guideline for your procedure.

_evicore.how: Your plan uses eviCore, which publishes its clinical guidelines free (you accept a terms click-through, no account). Pick your health plan, then the Musculoskeletal guideline for your surgery. If a guideline isn't posted, email reqcriteria@evicore.com and request it by name.

_turningpoint.how: Your plan delegates musculoskeletal surgery to TurningPoint, whose criteria are NOT published. Their own page says to submit the contact form naming your health plan to receive the correct policy. Do that, and put the same request in writing in your appeal - plans must supply the criteria used on request.

_interqual.how: Your plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a public document. You have a right to it anyway: federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to give you, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on for the denial. Ask in writing for 'the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination'.

_mcg.how: Your plan uses MCG, licensed software rather than a public document. Many plans run a no-login MCG viewer at {plan}.access.mcg.com - try that first. Otherwise ask in writing for 'the MCG guideline title, edition and criteria text applied to my determination'; the plan must provide it free of charge on request.

humana.how: Humana's criteria ARE public but they don't give any policy a permanent web address - links expire within hours. Open the search page and click the title for your surgery ('Knee Arthroplasty - Medicare Advantage', 'Knee Arthroscopy - Medicare Advantage', 'Shoulder Arthroscopy - Medicare Advantage'; change docbegin=H for hip, =S for shoulder). Save the PDF as soon as it opens.

highmark.how: Highmark's policy library looks like it needs JavaScript, but you can search it directly by adding your CPT code to the address: append ?q=27446 (or your code) to the search page URL. If the result is an 'S-' number in the 700s or above, that policy is MCG-based and only viewable in Highmark's licensed Clinical Guideline Tool - request it in writing instead.
highmark.source: securecms.highmark.com policy search + Highmark Medical Policy Update, Feb/Apr 2026

blue cross blue shield of north dakota.how: BCBSND writes and publishes its own criteria, free and login-free, but the search runs on JavaScript so a direct link often fails. Open the Medical Policy Search page and search by your CPT code.
blue cross blue shield of north dakota.warning: Some current policies sit under '/legacy-medical-policy/' URLs despite the name, and the Total Ankle policy S-9006-02 shows ARCHIVED as of 1 Jan 2024 - confirm the version banner before relying on one.

blue cross and blue shield of nebraska.how: Open 'Med Policy Blue', accept the disclaimer (no login), and search your CPT code. Important: if it returns 'No policies were found with a matching procedure code', BCBSNE states that means no preauthorization is required for that code - screenshot that result, it is strong evidence for your appeal.

blue cross blue shield of massachusetts.how: BCBSMA's policy library is public but its bot protection blocks automated tools - open it in a normal browser. Their orthopedic policies cover niche technologies; joint replacement reviews use InterQual, so also request the InterQual subset in writing.

cdphp.how: CDPHP publishes every policy as one large combined PDF (over 30 MB) - it will not open reliably on a phone. Download it on a computer and search the table of contents for your surgery.

health new england.how: HNE publishes a 'Musculoskeletal Surgery: Arthroplasty' clinical policy (revised effective 1 Apr 2026), but the PDF is blocked to automated tools - open the provider resources page in a normal browser and download it there.

sentara health plans.how: Sentara publishes separate Commercial, Medicaid and Medicare versions of each policy - make sure you download the one matching your plan type. Relevant titles: 'Lumbar Fusion - Surgical 118', 'Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion - Surgical 117', 'Lumbar Discectomy - Surgical 120', 'Total Ankle Replacement - Surgical 96'.

security health plan.how: Joint and spine surgery go through eviCore, whose guidelines are public. Security Health also has its own 'Total Hip Replacement Surgery' policy on their PolicyTech site. Note their 'Back Surgical Procedures' and hip impingement policies now redirect to a Sanford Health login - request those in writing.

medicaid.how: Most state Medicaid programs publish the rules for HOW a decision must be made but not the medical criteria for a specific surgery - those usually sit with your managed-care plan or its review vendor. Ask your plan in writing for 'the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization', and copy your state Medicaid agency. Massachusetts, North Carolina and California are the exceptions - they publish real procedure criteria.
